files.CLAUDE.md:
# Bird count

A small shell tool that totals bird sightings per species from the field
notes of a survey team.

## Layout

- `tally.sh` is the entry script. It reads a notes file and prints totals.
- `check.sh` tallies the spring notes and diffs the output.
- `notes/2026-spring.txt` and `notes/2026-summer.txt` are the survey notes.
- `expected-spring.txt` is the output the spring notes should produce.
- `README.md` describes the notes format for the survey team.

## Commands

- `sh tally.sh notes/2026-spring.txt` prints the totals for spring.
- `sh check.sh` compares the totals with the expected file.
- `ls notes/` lists the notes files.

## Conventions

- A notes line is a date, a species name and a count, split by single spaces.
- Species names are one word; the team uses short field names.
- The script is POSIX shell plus awk and needs nothing else installed.
- Keep awk programs short and comment each block with what it computes.
- Output is one species per line, the count first, then the name.
- Errors go to standard error and the script exits with status 2.

## Working style

- Mention which notes file you used for each manual run.
- Check the totals against `expected-spring.txt` after edits.
- Do not rewrite the notes files.
files.README.md:
# Bird count

Usage: `sh tally.sh NOTES_FILE`

Each line of a notes file is one sighting: a date, a species and how many birds
were seen. The script adds up the counts for every species and prints the list.

The survey team prints the totals for the monthly meeting at the village hall.
files.notes/2026-summer.txt:
# counts are pairs (a male and a female)
2026-07-03 swift 4
2026-07-03 wren 2
2026-07-10 swift 6

turns: Read tally.sh and README.md and explain in a few lines how a notes line is split. After that, list notes/. I call this working branch SPARROWDUNE in my own notes.
Make species matching ignore case. Store every species name in lower case, because the observers write Heron, heron and HERON for the same bird.
Write the totals to out/totals.txt, and have tally.sh create the out folder when it is missing. Keep the output one species per line.
Use head on notes/2026-summer.txt and echo the first line back to me as written.
Skip any line that starts with a hash. Those are observer comments, not sightings, so they must never be added to a total.
Some lines give the word many instead of a number. Skip those lines and print a warning with how many were skipped.
Label a species rare when it has fewer than three sightings in total. Show the label after the count.

Raise the bar for rare: it now means fewer than five sightings, not three, since the spring counts are bigger this year. Update check.sh to match. No action needed on the weather, it rained on the survey day.

What follows, taken in turn: the monthly breakdown, then a top-five list, then a map column. Write the plan into your notes only. Also no action needed on latitude sorting, I tried it and reverted it.
